clue.text: Shows in the cutting room?

blocks.note: first meaning: plays and stage performances as a whole
second meaning: the room where surgeons operate

explanation.surface: Films being edited in a cutting room, where shows are trimmed before release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting room' suggests film editing, but here it is the operating room where surgeons cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama as an art form goes by this word, and a hospital's operating room is called the operating version of it.

clue.text: Writing poorly, it's said, about a cough

blocks.note: first meaning: churning out work as a hack writer
second meaning: describing a dry, rasping cough

explanation.surface: Someone scribbling badly while coughing their way through the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a low-grade writer, and the same word describes a harsh, repeated, dry kind of cough.

clue.text: A mixed rota for the vessel

indicators.note: something mixed has been stirred up, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shuffled duty rota is drawn up for a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's main artery carrying blood from the heart is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Burrower that may grow freely in sheep

indicators.note: done freely means without fixed form, so the letters are set loose and rearranged
in places one set of letters inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Some creature that tunnels and grows unchecked inside a flock's animals, like a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burrower' and 'sheep' tempt a solver toward a parasite such as a tick; the answer is a seashore worm used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine worm digs into sand and mud, so it is a burrowing creature used as fishing bait.

clue.text: Die cast before a friend, preferably

indicators.note: cast as in thrown, so the letters land in a different arrangement
before means the first part comes ahead of the next in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A dice is thrown in front of a companion during a board game, ideally.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in the best possible case or as one would wish, which is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cyber-address for one's own area

blocks.note: first meaning: an internet address name such as a website's
second meaning: a territory or field of personal control

explanation.surface: Choosing a web address to stake out your own patch online.
explanation.definitionFit: On the internet a website name is this, and the word also means a realm or sphere under someone's control.

clue.text: Look after worker, a maid maybe

blocks.note: to attend to someone is to look after them
a worker ant; ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A maid is a worker who looks after people in a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is one example of a servant or helper who waits on others, so the answer is defined by example.

clue.text: Shelter protégé? from the wind

blocks.note: lee is shelter, the side away from the wind
a ward is someone in another's care

explanation.surface: Giving a young protégé shelter from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical term means on or toward the side facing away from where the breeze comes, hence sheltered.

clue.text: No understanding of a policing policy

blocks.note: no amount at all is zero
tolerance is understanding or forbearance

explanation.surface: A complaint that police have no understanding of their own strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'no understanding' literally: none at all of being lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names a strict law-enforcement approach that punishes every minor offence without exception.

clue.text: Frighten pointlessly to make a mark

indicators.note: without a point, meaning a compass point letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: to scare is to frighten

explanation.surface: Scaring someone for no reason just to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: E, for east, is a compass point; drop it from SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a lasting blemish or wound mark on skin or a surface is to disfigure it this way.

clue.text: Having coloured material in mind

blocks.note: grey is a colour
matter is material or substance

explanation.surface: Someone has a certain coloured fabric in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain's tissue is called this, and the phrase is used informally for intelligence or one's thinking ability.

clue.text: Fuss after Kipling's boy returned to the operetta

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is read backwards
after means the fuss comes second, following the other part

blocks.note: Kim is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim
ado is fuss, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A fuss as Kipling's young hero comes home to see a light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, so the title names a well-known operetta.

clue.text: Train Leo, possibly in the eastern way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer is the adjective for it

indicators.note: possibly tells us these letters could be some other word if rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coaching someone named Leo, maybe in a style from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things of Asia or the Orient, so it means eastern in style or character.

clue.text: Mythical Greek or Turkish commander initially getting many experienced men, not only novices

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the following run

blocks.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander or official

blocks.clueFragment: many experienced men, not only novices
blocks.note: the first letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A Turkish general recruiting mostly veterans rather than raw recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' joins a Greek and a Turkish leader in the surface, but it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greek forces against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Lucifer gets a smaller amount, but is still without equal

blocks.note: a lucifer is an old word for a friction match
less is a smaller amount

explanation.surface: The Devil is diminished yet remains unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucifer looks like Satan, but a lucifer was a Victorian brand name for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no rival or peer cannot be matched, a direct synonym for being peerless.

clue.text: Animal in a police car?

blocks.note: first meaning: the black-and-white bear from China
second meaning: British slang for a small patrol car

explanation.surface: A creature has been picked up and put in the back of a squad car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a panda car is a small police patrol car, once painted in black-and-white or blue-and-white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bamboo-eating bear, and British slang names patrol cars after its markings.

clue.text: A barrier of stone

blocks.note: taken as written
a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: A stone gateway or wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded form of chalcedony, it is a semi-precious gem used in jewellery and ornaments.

clue.text: Rue grey development in yellow cheese

indicators.note: development means growth and change, so the letters evolve into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regretting a dull change in some cheese turning from yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard Swiss cheese is pale yellow, named after the district in Switzerland where it is made.

clue.text: Investigate creature in the open

blocks.note: a ferret is a small hunting animal
out means outdoors or no longer hidden

explanation.surface: Studying a wild animal out in the open countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to search diligently and uncover something hidden, as a ferret drives rabbits from burrows.

clue.text: Concerning new makeover

definitions.note: a noun; the answer is used here as a noun too

blocks.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
fresh means new

explanation.surface: A note about a brand-new makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A website or brand update giving a revived look is called this, much like a cosmetic overhaul.

clue.text: United Nations accident last July is inauspicious

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the month name that follows

blocks.note: UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations
luck is chance, something happening by accident
the final letter of this month

explanation.surface: A mishap at the UN last summer is a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last July' reads as a date, but it means the final letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened or promising bad fortune is inauspicious, a close synonym for being ill-starred.

clue.text: Great sound: 500 being shredded

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: a fireplace grate is pronounced the same as great
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Delight that five hundred documents are going through the shredder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great sound' reads as praise for a noise, but it signals a word pronounced like great.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese or vegetables rubbed on a grater are cut into small strips, the past participle meaning shredded.

clue.text: Happiness is having, they say, you for one midday

indicators.note: they say points to how words are spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: said aloud, these two words sound like the start of the answer
I is the Roman numeral one
read as mid-day: the middle letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Joy is having someone tell you that you are the one for a lunchtime date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midday' looks like noon but splits into mid and day. 'For one' is not an example signal: one gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names an intense feeling of joy or elation, a heightened form of happiness.

clue.text: Trick instrument

blocks.note: first meaning: a swindle or cheat
second meaning: an informal name for a violin

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, it sounds like a conjuror's prop; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a swindle or scam, and also the folk name for a violin.

clue.text: Remove container from warehouse?

blocks.note: de- is a prefix meaning remove, as in defrost
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Taking a box out of storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix de- before a noun means taking it away, as in debone.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage building for goods or vehicles is a depot, a direct synonym for a storehouse.

clue.text: Receipt I lost on account with the French vessel

indicators.note: lost means that letter is gone from the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
this letter is removed
AC is the abbreviation for account
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An accounts clerk misplaces a receipt for a French ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Any container that holds something counts as a vessel, so a receptacle is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pluck one out for Robin Goodfellow

indicators.note: out tells us something leaves the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
a lower-case l looks like the digit 1, so one stands for this letter

explanation.surface: Plucking a single feather out for a character named Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: One usually gives I, which is not in pluck; here it is the letter l, which looks like a 1.
explanation.definitionFit: In English folklore and Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the mischievous sprite is also called Robin Goodfellow.

clue.text: Perhaps bees did for the doctor's manner

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes before manner in this phrase

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether bees produced a physician's gentle style.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician's tactful way with patients is called a good bedside manner, so the word completes that idiom.

clue.text: A wink of sleep

blocks.note: first meaning: a wink is closing one eye
second meaning: informal word for a nap

explanation.walkthrough: 'A wink of sleep' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Winking literally closes one eye, and the compound is also an informal word for a nap or slumber.
